title: CogSecSkills: Multiharness Agentic Skills for Cognitive Security
description: A defensive, educational, harness-neutral library of 100 agentic tool-use skills for Cognitive Security and analytic tradecraft (Structured Analytic Techniques, source verification, deception detection, critical review), with configured structural adapters for Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes, with a registry, an AGEINT educational upstream, and machine-checkable conformance.
release_name: v1.8.0 — reliability, modular runtime, and coherent archives

methods.name: Plan/Build/Teach architecture: registry, definitions, skills tree, AGEINT
methods.description: Separates a catalogue registry, canonical per-skill definitions, a harness-facing skills tree, and the AGEINT educational upstream.
methods.evidence: A description of the Plan/Build/Teach architecture that keeps registry/, skills/, and docs/ageint/ coherent.

methods.name: Harness-neutral skill contract over a closed set of eight tool verbs
methods.description: Each skill may use only neutral verbs (read, search, write, exec, reason, web, delegate, ask), bound per harness through adapters.
methods.evidence: A harness-neutral skill contract based on a closed set of tool verbs: read, search, write, exec, reason, web, delegate, and ask.

methods.name: Deterministic rendering into Claude, Codex, and Hermes adapters
methods.description: Renders each canonical definition into a spec, skill description, workflow, and one adapter per configured harness.
methods.evidence: The same skill can be rendered into the default Claude, Codex, and Hermes adapter language, or into an additional configured harness

methods.name: Automated anti-boilerplate per-skill quality audit
methods.description: Requires a skill-specific quality bundle and rejects generic or reused negative controls, rubrics, evidence and privacy entries.
methods.evidence: It also rejects repeated confidence-rubric, evidence-requirement, and privacy/legal entries, requires evidence requirements to label evidence and inference

methods.name: Evidence ladder: 28 scenario fixtures and per-skill worked examples
methods.description: Checks curated safe and unsafe scenarios against the local router and verifies one reviewed worked example per skill.
methods.evidence: scenarios/defensive_readiness.yaml contains 28 curated fixtures: two safe defensive requests and two unsafe refusal/redirect probes for each of the seven groups.

key_findings: The generated catalogue reports one hundred implemented skills across seven taxonomy groups, from Structured Analytic Techniques to Research and Synthesis Methods.

The author describes a local quality gate, explicitly 'not a safety proof', that can show all 100 skills include group-aware defensive boundaries and skill-specific governance entries in the current repository state.
The worked-example gate verifies exact 100-skill coverage; the examples are expected-answer shapes, not live model transcripts.
The author states the evidence is local conformance only and does not establish operational effectiveness, adversary coverage, user outcomes, or superiority over other libraries.
The deterministic gates do not show that a live runtime will select the same skill, use tools correctly, or answer well in the field.
key_findings_evidence: The live generated catalogue reports one hundred implemented skills across seven taxonomy groups
This is a local quality gate, not a safety proof. It can show that all 100 skills include group-aware defensive boundaries,
These examples are expected-answer shapes, not live model transcripts.
It does not establish real-world operational effectiveness, adversary coverage, user outcomes, or comparative superiority over other skill libraries.
The gates do not show that a live runtime will select the same skill, use tools correctly, or produce a high-quality answer in the field.
